title: I'm an arachnophobe and a tester, and AI finally let me make the spider horror game I always wanted
author: False_Geologist_7739
selftext:
![video](wpbnctqc353i1 "Cozy days. Wrong nights.maybe ")

Hi all! I've been in software testing for 20+ years, and I tried to make my own game more times than I can count. I always got stuck somewhere. On the side I write horror novels, mostly about spiders and dinosaurs.

I have arachnophobia. Despite that, or because of it, I always wanted to play a spider horror game that actually gives you goosebumps. Mixing it with calm, cozy gameplay (cozy horror) gave me what I was looking for: calm, then scared, then chill again, then dread.

This is what came out of it: **Eight Legs, Seven Nights**. You spend the week before Christmas in your aunt's snowed-in house, looking after her 13 spiders. Feeding, care and chores by day, a film with the cat in the evening. The nights are a different story: a different nightmare every night. Five endings, a built-in arcade game, five languages. Out on Steam on Dec 2; the demo and the trailer are up now.

The tools, since that's what this sub is for: Unity. Most of the code was written by Claude Code; I designed, tested, code-reviewed a lot, then re-tested, through an 800+ bug backlog. A scripted bot plays the whole week every night and logs problems with screenshots; as a tester, that's the part I'm proudest of. Some of the images are ChatGPT + Midjourney. The sound effects and the voice-over are ElevenLabs (there's a Mumble setting if you'd rather not hear AI voices). The 3D house, the spiders' behaviour, the story and the scares are hand-made.

I know AI is divisive, and I agree with a lot of the criticism. It's going to make my own job redundant too, slowly or quickly. But like every new technology, you either accept it and adapt, or you stand at the side of the road and watch the industry drive past. Used responsibly, I think it makes things possible that were impossible before.

Steam: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/2801310?utm\_source=reddit&utm\_campaign=aigamedev](https://store.steampowered.com/app/2801310?utm_source=reddit&utm_campaign=aigamedev)

All feedback welcome. Hit me! :)

PS: fun fact, the house is inspired by the Home Alone house.

comments.author: unfamily_friendly
comments.body: For some reason i imagine a horror game where there's a tiny tiny spider, couple pixels wide, and OP pointing at it, crying and saying "This is a horror beyond human comprehension"

replies.author: False_Geologist_7739
replies.body: Not far off. On night 2 a hand-sized cobalt blue gets out of her tank and you have to catch her under a wine glass, in the dark, with a torch. I've tested that scene a few hundred times and I still flinch. The big one comes later.

comments.author: BaconMarconi
comments.body:
oh my god, that's a hard pass.

Saw "Arachnophobia" when I was eight... gave me life long trauma 🤣

replies.author: False_Geologist_7739
replies.body:
Ha, fair. Arachnophobia is the reason this game exists. I saw it at about the same age and then watched it maybe a hundred times, so we took opposite lessons from it.

No hard feelings on the pass. If it helps, the jump scares can be switched off and the spiders mostly just want to be fed. Mostly.

replies.author: BaconMarconi
replies.body:
sweet baby jesus, you watched that film a hundred times? even the thought of that makes me shiver

I'm bailing on this thread rn 🤣

replies.author: False_Geologist_7739
replies.body: 100 is a rough count. Could be more. Go in peace, and check your shoes.
